title: An optimized proximity ligation assay to detect telomere dysfunction induced foci in human and mouse cells
protocol: Wash cells with 1× PBS at 20°C–25°C.
Dissociate cultured cells with Trypsin-EDTA for 5 minutes.
Neutralize cells with trypsin neutralization solution or an equal volume of cell culture medium supplemented with 10% or 20% Bovine Calf Serum or Fetal Bovine Serum.
Suspend cells by pipetting the cell culture medium several times.
Spin at 300 g for 3 minutes at 20°C–25°C using a benchtop centrifuge to pellet cells.
Count cells using a hemocytometer manually or a cell counter.
Resuspend cells in a 35 mm plate with a 10 mm collagen-coated coverslip, using 2 mL fresh medium to obtain approximately 150,000 cells/mL.
Leave the plate at 20°C–22°C for 30 minutes.
Incubate cells at 37°C for 6 hours to several days until desired confluency is reached.
Spin suspension cells (e.g., peripheral blood mononuclear cells) onto a poly-lysine coated slide using a cytospin centrifuge at 72.26 g for 3 minutes.
Wash cells with 1× PBS for 3 × 5 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Treat cells with 100 μL of cytoskeletal (CSK) solution for 5 minutes on ice.
Remove the CSK solution gently using a pipette.
Repeat treatment with CSK solution for another 5 minutes on ice.
Wash cells with 1× PBS for 3 × 5 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Treat cells with 100 μL of pre-cooled 100% MeOH for 20 minutes at −20°C.
Pause the experiment after fixing cells.
Store fixed cells in 1× PBS at 4°C for up to 24 hours or transfer to 70% ethanol and store at -20°C for up to one week.
Seal plates with parafilm during storage to prevent drying out.
Warm stored plates to 20°C-25°C before proceeding.
Wash cells with 1× PBS for 3 × 5 minutes at 20°C-25°C.
Block cells in 100 μL Blocking solution (provided by Duolink® In Situ PLA® Probe kit) for 1 hour at 37°C.
Alternatively, block cells in 10% BSA in PBS-T.
Prepare hybridization mixture containing the telomere—biotin probe from Integrated DNA Technologies.
Tap off blocking solution and add hybridization mix to central coverslip.
Place plate inside a pre-heated humidified chamber.
Preheat hybridization oven to reach 80°C.
Incubate plate in humidified chamber (approximately 85% humidity) at 80°C for 3 minutes.
Incubate the plate in a humidified chamber for 2 hours at 20°C–25°C.
Wash cells with hybridization wash buffer for 3 × 5 minutes.
Wash cells with 1× PBS for 3 × 5 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Thaw reagents besides enzymes at 20°C–25°C and vortex before use.
Keep enzymes at −20°C and add to the reaction mix before use.
Dilute 5× stock solutions with high purity water before use.
Perform all incubations in a humidity chamber.
Cover 1 cm² sample area on the coverslip with a 40 μL reaction volume.
Use an open droplet reaction for the entire process.
Ensure that the entire reaction area is always covered by reagents/solutions.
Discard the blocking solution.
Wash cells with 1× PBS for 3 × 5 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Dilute primary antibodies to suitable concentrations in Antibody diluent and add solutions to each sample (50 μL/coverslip).
Incubate the plate in a humidity chamber ∼12 hours overnight at 4°C or 1 hour at 37°C.
Mix and dilute PLA probe MINUS stock, PLA probe PLUS stock, and antibody buffer in Antibody diluent for a total volume of 40 μL reaction.
Allow the mixture to sit for 20 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Tap off the primary antibody solution from the coverslip.
Wash the plate with 2 mL 1× Wash Buffer A on a shaker with gentle orbital shaking for 3 × 5 min at 20°C–25°C.
Tap off excess wash buffer after each washing cycle.
Add 40 μL PLA probe solution to the plate.
Preheat a humidity chamber to 37°C.
Incubate the plate in pre-heated humidity chamber for 1 h at 37°C.
Dilute the Ligation solution 1:5 in ddH2O, e.g., mix 8 μL of 5× Ligation solution with 31 μL of ddH2O for a total volume of 40 μL.
Tap off PLA probe solution from the coverslip at the bottom of the plate.
Wash the plate with 2 mL 1× Duolink In Situ Wash Buffer A for 3 × 10 min under gentle agitation on a shaker.
Discard excess wash buffer after each washing cycle.
Add Ligase to Ligation solution at a 1:40 dilution, e.g., add 1 μL of Ligase to 39 μL of diluted Ligation solution and vortex thoroughly.
Add 40 μL Ligation-Ligase solution to each coverslip.
Incubate the plate in pre-heated humidity chamber for 30 min at 37°C.
Dilute the Amplification stock 1:5 in ddH2O.
Tap off the Ligation-Ligase solution from the coverslip at the bottom of the plate.
Wash the plate with 2 ml 1× Duolink InSitu Wash Buffer A for 2 × 3 min under gentle agitation on a shaker.
Tap off all wash solution after the last wash.
Add the Polymerase to the Amplification solution at a 1:80 dilution and vortex.
Add the Amplification-Polymerase solution to each coverslip.
Incubate the plate in a pre-heated humidity chamber for 100 min at 37°C, covered with foil.
Tap off the Amplification-Polymerase solution from the coverslip.
Wash the plate in 2 mL 1× DuolinkInSitu Wash Buffer B for 4 × 10 minutes.
Wash the plate in 0.01 × Wash Buffer B for 5 minutes.
Wash the plate in 2 mL 1× PBS for 1 × 5 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Dilute secondary antibodies conjugated with fluorophores to suitable concentrations, e.g., 1:500 in Antibody Diluent.
Add 40 μL of secondary antibody solution to each coverslip.
Incubate the plate in a humidity chamber ∼12 hours at 4°C or 1 hour at 37°C.
Tap off the secondary antibody solution from the plate.
Wash the plate with 2 mL 1× PBS-T on a shaker for 3 × 5 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Let the coverslip dry briefly at 20°C–25°C in the dark.
Mount the coverslip onto the slide using ProLong™ Gold Antifade mounting solution with DAPI (0.01 mg/mL).
Seal the edges with nail polish.
Capture images from 20–30 fields per slide in z-stacks using a confocal fluorescent microscope with a 100× (oil) objective.
Use a DAPI filter for nuclear staining.
Use a Cy5 filter for detection of PLA signals when the DuolinkFarRed detection kit is used.
Use FITC, Cy3, or Texas Red filters to detect different targets such as telomeric markers and DDR proteins.
Adjust brightness and contrast of captured raw images using software like ImageJ or Adobe Photoshop.
Apply the same adjustment settings to all images from the experiment.
Capture signals in z-stacks for each channel.
Avoid binning during acquisition of each channel.
Adjust exposure time to maintain good signal-to-noise ratio across all channels without oversaturation.
Ensure DAPI signal intensity versus IF, Telomere FISH, and PLA signals is no less than 5:1 ratio.
Count TIF numbers per nucleus in PLA images, aiming for ≥5 TIFs/cell.
Quantify the percentage of cells with ≥5 TIFs.
Verify TIF signals by colocalization of DDR proteins (such as 53BP1 and γ-H2AX) and telomeric proteins (such as TRF1 and TRF2).
Colocalize most TIF signals by PLA with those by IF or IF-Telomere FISH to confirm successful PLA procedure.
Clean slides with 70% ethanol if stored at 4°C or −20°C before imaging.
Warm slides at 20°C–25°C for 1 hour or at 37°C for 10 minutes to prevent condensation on the surface of slides.
